releases.body:
### VS Code companion 0.1.6: fast resume vs session picker

* The **Perun TUI** status-bar item now fast-resumes the newest TUI chat — the
  dashboard's **Run** — instead of opening a picker.
* **Perun: Choose TUI session…** (`perun.openTui`) is the picker: resume latest,
  any of the last 50 sessions (headless ones labelled, never auto-selected), or
  start a new session. `perun.openTui` keeps its id, so existing keybindings
  still work.
* Companion 0.1.6, suite 10/10.

### VS Code companion 0.1.5: the session picker mirrors the dashboard

* **“Resume latest” now means the newest TUI chat.** A session whose first run
  was a headless job (a coroutine, a one-off run) is labelled `headless run`,
  stays explicitly selectable, and is never auto-selected — the same rule the
  dashboard's Run button uses.
* Each entry shows time, status, origin (`TUI chat` / `headless run`) and the
  OpenCode session id; the list covers the last 50 sessions, and “Start a new
  session” is always present.
* `src/session_pick.js` mirrors `web/js/session_pick.js` and is covered by
  `tests/session_pick.test.js` (companion suite now 10 tests).

### Context governor: measurable and bounded

* **Shadow mode is the default** (`context_governor_shadow`): the governor logs
  what it *would* compact, minute by minute, and never calls OpenCode until the
  operator turns shadow off. The Settings card shows the last pass
  ("checked 4 · would compact 1") and each event's cost delta.
* New limits: `context_governor_idle_minutes` (30; never touch a session whose
  usage snapshot is older), `context_governor_max_per_day` (6; hard ceiling on
  real compactions), and higher defaults (`150k` tokens, `100`-message cooldown)
  so a compaction has time to pay for itself.
* `settle()` closes the previous compaction's after-values as soon as the session
  is idle, independently of the next compact decision — so an active session can
  no longer starve the measurement and the three-strike self-disable actually
  fires. The disable is recorded as an activity row.
* The live-context estimate now handles both provider styles: Anthropic-style
  disjoint fields (`input + cache.read`) and OpenAI-style inclusive
  (`input`, cached is a subset).
* An active session is re-checked immediately before the compact call.

* **Boundary compaction works against a live OpenCode.** A body-less
  `POST /session/{id}/compact` is rejected with `Expected object`; the governor
  now sends `{}`. Verified against the running service (a real compaction
  message comes back).
* Two fast **Prepare** clicks reserve the download slot before the worker starts,
  so the second click gets a clean "a download is already running" instead of a
  job that fails immediately.
* The download progress poll stops when the Settings card is no longer on the
  page, and both Settings cards share one `/api/local-ai` fetch per render.
* Enabling **OpenCode small tasks** warns first when `opencode.json` contains
  comments (the rewrite drops them; a backup is kept).
* **The Local AI model is a picker** of the models the runtime reports (with
  sizes), with a "Custom / not installed" field for a tag that has not been
  pulled yet, instead of a free-text box.
* MCP output budgets cache the Settings read for 5 s instead of reading
  `config.json` on every tool call.

* **Settings no longer rewrites the OpenCode config on every save.**
  `set_small_model()` returns unchanged when the value already matches, so the
  dashboard's Save no longer creates a new `opencode.json.perun-backup-*` each
  time. A JSONC comment loss is now logged explicitly.
* **Downloads respect disk space.** `Prepare` refuses to start when the model
  store has less than 2 GB free (Ollama reports the real size only once the pull
  starts, so this is a safety net) and returns the free/required bytes.
* Cancelling an already-finished job no longer leaves its id in the in-memory
  cancellation set.
* The **OpenCode small tasks** toggle is disabled with an explanation when a
  custom endpoint is configured (OpenCode's `small_model` is provider-specific),
  and the Local AI card warns when the endpoint is not loopback: prompts from the
  local-AI consumers would leave the machine.

* **Local AI Test tolerates a cold model.** The probe now waits up to 60 s: the
  first call after a download loads the model from disk (tens of seconds), and a
  15 s timeout reported a working model as offline.

### Local AI: a small local model for bounded work

* New **Settings → Local AI** card: enable a local model (Ollama, LM Studio,
  vLLM — any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), choose the download policy (`auto`
  pulls through Ollama, `manual` prints the exact command), watch a pull with
  progress, and test the endpoint. Off by default; every consumer falls back to
  the previous behaviour when the model or runtime is unavailable.
* `perun/local_llm.py` is the only client: stdlib transport, an 8 s timeout,
  JSON-mode fallback for runtimes that reject `response_format`, a cached health
  probe, and it never raises. `perun/model_manager.py` drives Ollama
  (`/api/tags`, `/api/pull`, `/api/delete`) with a disk guard, one pull at a
  time, cancellation, and persisted job progress.
* Consumers: the changelog bullet after an executed proposal (shadow mode logs
  the locally generated line instead of using it) and OpenCode's own
  `small_model` for titles/small tasks (written through the backed-up config
  writer, removed when the toggle is turned off).
* New **Settings → Context** card: opt-in boundary compaction through OpenCode's
  `POST /session/{id}/compact`. It triggers on the live context size, respects a
  cooldown in messages, never touches an active session, records before/after
  rows, and disables itself when three compactions fail to shrink the context.
* Search and memory tools cap their output (`context_tool_budget_chars`,
  `context_memory_budget_chars`) with an explicit truncation marker; exact file
  reads are never truncated.
* Schema v27 adds `local_ai_jobs` and `context_events`.

* The VS Code companion package now ships its MIT license
  (`extensions/vscode/LICENSE`), so `vsce` no longer warns and the installed
  extension carries the license text.

* **Windows: paths with cmd metacharacters.** `_code_command()` quoted an
  argument only when it contained a space, so a VSIX under a path like
  `C:\R&D\…` was split at the `&` and `code` reported
  `Extension 'c:\…\perun' not found`. Every argument is now quoted; verified
  live with a `perun&co` directory.
* **Download validation is total.** The packaged manifest must be ≤ 1 MB
  (`ZipInfo.file_size`, so a zip bomb never expands into memory), and any decode
  failure — encryption, unsupported compression, truncation — is treated as
  "not the companion" instead of raising out of `perun install`.
* The `publish-companion` job runs the extension unit tests before it publishes,
  `perun install` no longer touches VS Code when the global install failed, and
  `--no-vscode-download` no longer claims a `--vscode` flag that does not exist.

### Windows: the companion install survives paths with spaces

* `install_vscode_extension()` passed `["cmd.exe", "/c", …]` to
  `subprocess.run`, which `cmd.exe` re-parses and de-quotes. With both the
  `code.cmd` shim (`…\Microsoft VS Code\…`) and the VSIX under a path with a
  space (a user name or install directory), it stripped the quotes and failed
  with `'…\Microsoft' is not recognized as an internal or external command`.
  The line is now wrapped in the extra quote pair `cmd.exe /c` expects, and a
  regression test pins it.

### Companion distribution hardening

* The VSIX is published by its own `publish-companion` workflow job, so a
  failing Windows or macOS installer build can no longer leave the release
  without a downloadable companion (that is how v0.14.2 shipped nothing).
* A downloaded VSIX must contain `extension/package.json` for
  `perun`/`perun-overseer`; a proxy page or a foreign archive is refused and
  never written to disk.
* `perun install` is a no-op when `code --list-extensions --show-versions`
  already reports the VSIX version (`--force` reinstalls), and
  `--no-vscode-download` restricts it to a local VSIX for offline installs.
* The Windows installer no longer copies the VSIX twice (`installer\vscode` is
  excluded from the recursive copy; the file is still installed to
  `{app}\vscode`), and `AGENTS.md` records that the companion is per-user and
  never installs VS Code.
